newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges calm, return to talks in Israel.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges calm, return to talks in Israel.

text.p: The White House on Thursday urged a return to calm and peace negotiations after bloody clashes between Israeli and Palestinian security forces on the West Bank and Gaza Strip.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry said President Bill Clinton would make a statement on the situation at midday on Thursday. "It's all cause for great concern," McCurry said.

Violence on Thursday took the death toll to 38 Arabs and 10 Israelis in two days of clashes, sparked by what Arabs called Israeli encroachment on Muslim holy places in Jerusalem. More than 300 Palestinians and 43 Israelis were reported wounded on Thursday.
McCurry said Clinton would urge Middle Eastern leaders to use their influence to return calm to Israel and the Arab territories.
He stopped short of calling Israel's opening of an archaeological tunnel near a Muslim holy site a provocative act, but came close.

"The administration believes that the parties should concentrate on implementing the agreements that they have reached, dealing with the issues that are outstanding between them, and that the parties should take no steps that raise new issues that cause complications in the very difficult, complicated discussions that they already have under way. It's clearly a new issue," he said.
